messages.subject: runMI / sem.mi with categorical data and multiply imputed data
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to fit a structural equation model with a binary outcome variable and cluster-robust standard errors and pool results for 5 previously imputed data sets. I do not get any error message, however using runMI, the coefficient for my latent construct is '0' and no standard errors are not displayed. So I guess, I am doing something wrong, but I cannot figure out what it is. Maybe someone can help me? I would really appreciate it!

Here's the code I ran:
(for the first imputed dataset)

sem1 <- 'genbild =~ t31300a_w3 + 1*t31300c_w3 + t31300e_w3 +
            t31300f_w3 + t31300g_w3 + t31300j_w3
                ueb10 ~ genbild '

fit <- sem(sem1, data = imp1, ordered="ueb10", cluster="ID_i")
summary(fit)

(for all 5 imputed datasets)

fit.mi <- runMI(data=impulist, sem1, chi="lmrr", ordered="ueb10",
                fun="sem", cluster="ID_i")
summary(fit.mi)

The output for the multiply imputed datasets looks as follows:

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: runMI / sem.mi with categorical data and multiply imputed data
parts:
On 12/04/2015 11:31 AM, Jen Lorenz wrote:
> I am trying to fit a structural equation model with a binary outcome
> variable and cluster-robust standard errors and pool results for 5
> previously imputed data sets.

I am afraid this will not work. lavaan (0.5-20) (nor lavaan.survey) can
currently handle the combination categorical data + cluster-robust errors.
> I do not get any error message
That is a bit strange indeed.
> fit <- sem(sem1, data = imp1, ordered="ueb10", cluster="ID_i")

Have you read the documentation for the sem() function? About the
cluster= argument, it says:

"cluster: Not used yet."

which of course is a bit silly. It is just a placeholder for things to
come. Currently (0.5-20), we need the lavaan.survey package to handle
clusters. But lavaan.survey (in fact, the survey package) can not handle
binary outcomes.

Mplus can handle this. And in stata, you can use gllamm, or perhaps even
gsem. If anyone knows about other possibilities, please let us know.

> summary(fit)
>
> (for all 5 imputed datasets)
>
> fit.mi <- runMI(data=impulist, sem1, chi="lmrr", ordered="ueb10",
> fun="sem", cluster="ID_i")
> summary(fit.mi)
>
> The output for the multiply imputed datasets looks as follows:

I am not sure why the runMI gives NA values. You may wish to contact the
authors of runMI for this.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: runMI / sem.mi with categorical data and multiply imputed data
parts:
Could you please try the semTools package from the following link?

https://github.com/simsem/semTools/raw/master/builds/semTools_0.4-10.tar.gz

Then, install the package from the following command:

install.packages("yoursemToolsFile", repos = NULL, type = "source")
